transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-10
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jade Lin (Redwood SE), Alex Gomez (ApexCloud Head Partnerships), Maya Singh (Solutions Architect), Liam O'Connor (CTO)

Summary:
Quick partner intro between Redwood and ApexCloud to understand partnership model (resell/integrate), technical fit for GPU hosting, and next steps for a pilot benchmarking run. Some notes on security, VPC/private deployments, and integration patterns.

Topics:
- Partner models (reseller, referral, co-sell)
- Technical fit: GPU types, autoscale, Dedicated vs Hosted, on-prem options
- Security: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs
- Benchmarks: latency targets, throughput, cost per token

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Samir from Redwood, i'm joined by Jade. quick round intro?
[00:12] Alex Gomez: Alex here, head of partnerships at ApexCloud. Maya and Liam are on as well. thanks for making time.
[00:18] Maya Singh: hi all, Maya - solutions architect. excited to talk through how we might partner.
[00:30] Jade Lin: great, quick agenda: 1) partner models 2) tech / infra fit 3) pilot/benchmarks 4) next steps. sound ok?
[00:40] Liam O'Connor: yep sounds good, we have a checklist i can share later.
[00:45] Samir Patel: cool. Alex, could you describe ApexCloud's GTM and the types of integrations you're looking for?
[00:55] Alex Gomez: Sure, we do managed GPU hosting across eu/us/apac, we sell to SaaS and enterprise customers. our channel is partner friendly, we want a few integration models - reseller where we operate Redwood Dedicated in our stack, or referral where we send customers to Redwood hosted. also curious about co-branding.
[01:15] Samir Patel: excellent. on the technical side, Jade, want to pick up?
[01:20] Jade Lin: Yep. quick question: what's your current fleet composition and orchestration? is it k8s, nomad? what GPUs?
[01:30] Maya Singh: mostly k8s, but we run a mix - A100 80GB, H100 in our newer zones, and some older A40s for lower tiers. we use custom autoscaler + internal quota.
[01:42] Jade Lin: ok that maps well. Redwood's runtime supports a bunch of kernels and will route based on model and seq length. for dedicated we typically run a reserved pool; for reseller model we can deploy a private control plane or run in your cloud with our private package.
[01:58] Maya Singh: when you say private package, do you mean we host the control plane or you manage it?
[02:05] Jade Lin: either. we offer a customer-managed control plane (private) or we can do a co-managed deployment where we run agents in your VPC and the control plane is customer-owned. some customers want full on-prem for compliance.
[02:18] Alex Gomez: good. security is huge for our enterprise accounts - SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, HSM options, audit logs - do you support those?
[02:28] Samir Patel: yes, we have SOC 2, SAML SSO and KMS integrations. audit logs and per-token tracing are in the console. i'll share the security pack after this.
[02:35] Liam O'Connor: and encryption at rest across your private deploy?
[02:40] Jade Lin: yes, customer-managed KMS/HSM supported for private, encrypted artifacts. for hosted we support envelope encryption and key rotation.
[02:48] Maya Singh: nice. on perf: typical enterprise ask - latency SLOs and cost. how does Redwood approach batching / kv cache / quantization?
[02:58] Jade Lin: we do continuous batching with workload-aware batching policies, KV cache for prefixes, and quantization profiles per-model. the runtime will pick kernels and quantization friendly execution based on architecture and seq length. that reduces token cost while keeping latency.
[03:15] Alex Gomez: do you have any sample numbers on A100 vs H100 for, say, a 4k context model?
[03:22] Jade Lin: depends on model but H100 is ~1.5-2x throughput for large contexts in our tests. i'll follow up with the perf sheet. note: we also recommend model variants for low-latency fallbacks.
[03:34] Samir Patel: one thing we often discuss with partners is routing policies - you can route by latency, cost or region. so ApexCloud could surface Redwood Dedicated as a higher SLA tier.
[03:46] Alex Gomez: that helps our sales motion. business question - pricing splits if we resell?
[03:51] Samir Patel: we have partner pricing tiers; i'll put the matrix in the deck. usually margin depends on commit level and support SLA.
[04:00] Maya Singh: on benchmarking, we'd want a pilot that tests throughput for 1k concurrent requests, a latency P95 target under 300ms for short prompts, and cost per 1M tokens.
[04:12] Jade Lin: good, we'll propose test cases. what models do you plan to run? open LLMs or proprietary?
[04:20] Liam O'Connor: customers run mix - Llama-2 variants, Orca smaller models for embedding-ish tasks, and some proprietary LLMs for internal. we also need to support tool-calling and streaming in some of our apps.
[04:33] Jade Lin: streaming and function/tool calling supported. the runtime supports meaty attention optimizations for tool-heavy flows.
[04:40] Alex Gomez: any red flags on our side that would prevent private deploy? like networking constraints or k8s versions?
[04:48] Jade Lin: we generally support k8s >=1.24 and standard CNI; for air-gapped we need some artifact transfer but it's supported. we'll capture specifics in the tech-deep-dive.
[04:58] Samir Patel: a quick note on quotas and autoscale - Redwood Dedicated has configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity. for reseller, we can map your existing quota layer.
[05:09] Maya Singh: good. customers also ask about observability - what does the console expose?
[05:15] Jade Lin: token-level cost/latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, traces and error analytics. we also integrate with datadog and opentelemetry dumps.
[05:24] Alex Gomez: perfect. competitors - we've been getting interest where customers compare to Scale and Paperspace - what are your differentiators?
[05:33] Samir Patel: we focus on production-grade inference: kernel selection, unified API across hosted/dedicated/private, and cost-aware controls (batching/quantization) plus rollout tooling. less about model hosting and more about predictable serving economics.
[05:49] Maya Singh: sounds good. technical question - if we co-locate Redwood runtime in our zones, how do updates work? can we schedule windows?
[05:57] Jade Lin: yes, updates are configurable, and we support canary rollouts and A/B tests with automatic fallback. you pick maintenance windows.
[06:05] Alex Gomez: for pilots we'd like to run a small footprint in 2 regions to evaluate cross-region routing, and then expand. cost/perf tradeoffs matter.
[06:14] Samir Patel: makes sense. Jade, anything else on benchmarks?
[06:18] Jade Lin: i'll draft a benchmark spreadsheet: workloads, seq lengths, model list (Llama-2-13B, Llama-2-70B, custom customer small models), concurrency, target metrics. include network variance scenarios.
[06:28] Maya Singh: please add a 95th percentile and tail-latency column. also include warm/cold cache runs since KV cache matters a lot for our use cases.
[06:36] Jade Lin: noted.
[06:38] Alex Gomez: commercial question - are you open to co-selling arrangements and joint logos?
[06:43] Samir Patel: absolutely. we have co-sell policies and partner tiers. i'll include the partner program slide.
[06:50] Liam O'Connor: from infra side we want to test model quantization benefits - some of our customers are sensitive to accuracy regressions. how do you monitor regressions?
[06:59] Jade Lin: Redwood Optimize has quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets/evals. we can run eval harnesses against baseline prompts to detect quality drop post-quantization.
[07:12] Maya Singh: great that's essential. any legal procurement red flags? minimum contract terms?
[07:18] Samir Patel: standard partner MSA, we can be flexible on term length for pilots. for enterprise private deployments we usually do an annual licensing + support fee. procurement can be triaged after pilot.
[07:29] Alex Gomez: ok. timeline wise, what's realistic for a pilot?
[07:33] Samir Patel: once we have fleet details and a test plan, we can spin up a pilot in ~2-3 weeks. private deployments add extra time for networking and approvals.
[07:42] Maya Singh: that works.
[07:44] Alex Gomez: any specific network ports or egress rules for private agents?
[07:49] Jade Lin: minimal outbound to our control plane endpoints, TLS only; i will extract a network checklist and share.
[07:57] Samir Patel: okay next steps recap - i'll send partner deck and pricing; Jade will send benchmark plan and schedule deep-dive; Maya will send fleet spec and SSO contact.
[08:10] Alex Gomez: perfect. any blocker for us to sign NDA or start data sharing?
[08:15] Samir Patel: no blocker, we can do NDA quickly. i'll include legal contact in the follow-up.
[08:22] Maya Singh: quick question about telemetry retention - how long do you retain logs by default?
[08:27] Jade Lin: default is 90 days for the console; extended retention is an add-on. we'll note retention options in the security pack.
[08:36] Alex Gomez: OK great.
[08:38] [Cross-talk] everyone: thanks!

[49:35] Liam O'Connor: thanks all.
[49:40] Samir Patel: thanks, speak soon.

End of transcript.
